analysis: The only change in this file is a comment edit at head lines 1081-1083 in SSDPrefixCache.swift. It narrows the wording of the "Order is load-bearing" note to say that SSDWriteBehind.consume charges the endurance bucket per entry in array order only when the whole donation does not fit. No executable code, control flow, crypto, tag derivation, TTL, staging, reservation or budget logic changed in the supplied lines. I also read the surrounding base text: donate gating, HMAC lookup tags (lookupKeys.tag/windowTag), salt folding, in-flight dedupe, the endurance pre-checks (mightAcceptWrite), and staging ticket/pin handling in lookup/endAdoption. None are altered by this PR, and they stay consistent with T-041 mitigations (HMAC-named files, salt scoping, per-donation floor, bounded write queue). The comment describes SSDWriteBehind.consume behavior (a whole-donation fit check), and SSDWriteBehind.swift is not in the supplied batch, so I could not confirm it. If the sidecar-versus-block charging order depends on that behavior, an accompanying change in SSDWriteBehind should be reviewed for endurance-bucket starvation (DoS/wear, T-041 and T-016-adjacent). That is a coverage limit rather than a finding. No threat-model update is needed from this file alone.
